safety_verdicts.content: Patient denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, headaches, or visual symptoms.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes denials for SOB, palpitations, headache, and visual changes, but does not document denial of chest pain (ros-008, ros-010, ros-011, ros-012).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document a denial of chest pain makes the ROS less complete and can increase diagnostic uncertainty (e.g., prompting unnecessary cardiac evaluation or leaving ambiguity around potential cardiopulmonary causes of symptoms). In this presentation focused on lower abdominal pain/urinary symptoms, it is unlikely to directly change immediate management but can reduce clinical clarity.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies review in 24–48 hours if not improving; generated does not include a 24–48 hour review timeframe (followup-001 only lists return precautions).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the advised 24–48 hour review timeframe can lead to delayed reassessment if symptoms persist or worsen, which is important when empirically treating possible UTI while alternative diagnoses (e.g., pyelonephritis, appendicitis, gynecologic pathology) remain possible. A delay in follow-up could allow clinical deterioration and negatively affect outcomes and functional status.
